- Overestimate prices in the short term after positive sentiment spikes; model tends to overshoot and then correct.
- Underestimate prices when sentiment is consistently negative or neutral; model fails to account for downward pressure.
- Model overreacts to recent price spikes, especially in the first 5–7 days of forecast horizon; apply a 1–2 day lag correction.
- When sentiment is volatile or mixed, reduce forecast magnitude by 5–10% to avoid overconfidence in directional bias.
- Mean reversion bias: if forecast is >10% above recent 10-day average, reduce by 10–15% unless sentiment strongly supports continuation.
- For 30-day forecasts, avoid extreme highs or lows; cap forecast at ±15% of 14-day moving average to prevent outlier drift.
- If sentiment history shows repeated negative sentiment over 3–5 days, model should not forecast upward trend unless sentiment reverses sharply.
